subsystems.name: Sampling kit
subsystems.role: collects microbial DNA from the skin surface in a form stable enough to post to a lab.

subsystems.name: Sequencing and analysis
subsystems.role: reads the microbial DNA and identifies which bacteria are present and in what relative amounts.

subsystems.name: Formulation base
subsystems.role: a neutral, stable serum that can accept added actives without separating or spoiling.

subsystems.name: Active ingredient library
subsystems.role: a set of prebiotics, probiotics or postbiotics that can be selected to shift the skin flora.

subsystems.name: Custom blending and filling
subsystems.role: combines the base and chosen actives in the right proportions and packages the final serum.

buildSteps.title: Order and sample collection
buildSteps.detail: The customer orders a kit online, swabs a defined area of skin, and returns the sample to a laboratory.

buildSteps.title: DNA extraction and sequencing
buildSteps.detail: The lab extracts microbial DNA from the swab and sequences marker genes such as 16S rRNA, or in some cases the whole metagenome.

buildSteps.title: Bioinformatics analysis
buildSteps.detail: Software compares the sequences to a reference database to list which microbial groups are present and estimate their relative abundance and diversity.

buildSteps.title: Deficiency mapping
buildSteps.detail: An algorithm flags groups that fall outside a reference range and links them to skin concerns such as dryness, sensitivity or breakouts.

buildSteps.title: Formulation selection
buildSteps.detail: A rules-based or machine-learning system chooses actives from the library that are intended to encourage beneficial groups or suppress undesirable ones.

buildSteps.title: Compounding
buildSteps.detail: A technician or automated system mixes a standard serum base with the selected actives in measured amounts, following a batch record.

buildSteps.title: Filling and packaging
buildSteps.detail: The serum is filled into bottles, labelled with the customer's formula, and shipped with usage instructions.

buildSteps.title: Follow-up testing
buildSteps.detail: After several weeks the customer may send a second swab so the lab can compare the microbial profile and adjust the next batch.

prerequisites.why: it reads the microbial DNA from a skin swab quickly and cheaply enough for a consumer service.

prerequisites.tech: Reference databases of the skin microbiome
prerequisites.why: many skin bacteria are catalogued, but their roles and normal ranges are still being mapped.
links between specific microbes and skin health are often correlational; causality is not always established.
a serum must stay stable and safe while carrying actives that may be sensitive to heat, oxygen or microbes.
making one unique batch per customer at scale requires flexible factories and tracking from swab to bottle.
rules on custom-made products and microbiome claims vary by country and are still evolving.

pathway.milestone: Niche commercial services offer 16S sequencing and a personalized serum based on broad microbial categories.
pathway.unlocks: Early adopters can try tailored care, and large datasets of skin microbiomes begin to accumulate.

pathway.milestone: Metagenomic and functional analysis become standard, linking specific strains or metabolites to skin outcomes.
pathway.unlocks: More precise formulations with actives that have a clearer mechanistic rationale.

pathway.milestone: Clinical trials compare microbiome-tailored serums with standard products for conditions such as acne or eczema.
pathway.unlocks: Medical credibility, clearer claims, and broader adoption beyond the wellness market.

pathway.milestone: Integration with other personal data (genetics, environment, lifestyle) and real-time skin sensors.
pathway.unlocks: Dynamic, predictive skincare that adjusts as the skin and its microbes change.

pathway.milestone: On-demand, local manufacturing of personalized serums at pharmacy or home scale.
pathway.unlocks: Zero-inventory, highly responsive supply with minimal shipping.
